_schema: One station, in the shape M3 fixed. M6 adds `when` on a canvas: the ISO date behind the holder's own words, so tools/station.py can ask whether a canvas is inside its station's span.
title: The Potato Eaters
_canvases:
One canvas, and it is the floor of the piece. DESIGN 7: a low dark room, one oil lamp, five figures, coffee, and you can barely see -- so that everything after it can fly.

There is no lamp in this station. The lamp is in the painting, and the dark is in the paint, and putting a light source in this room would be relighting a Van Gogh -- which is exactly the mistake M5 caught and measured at station 5, where lighting the built surfaces by their own face normals ruled a bright band across the Bedroom at the wall-floor crease. The station is dark because the canvas is dark, and BUILD.md M6 gives the number: its area-weighted mean lightness against the corridor's.

canvases.title: The Potato Eaters
canvases.note: 114 by 82 cm, the largest canvas in the piece. The six numbers of the room are authored -- M5 established that they have to be, because tools/room.py cannot recover a stable vanishing point from a Van Gogh interior and its calibration says what that would have taken. What is worth saying is which of the six were read off the canvas and which were not. Three were: the back wall's left edge at 0.06 and right edge at 0.93 are where the room's corners are in the picture, and 0.17 is where the beams meet the wall. Two were not, because they cannot be -- the floor of this room is behind the table and is not in the painting at all, so the row where the back wall meets it is invented, and so is the row the window's axis crosses. They were chosen by running M5's arithmetic backwards until the room came out the size a Brabant cottage room is: 4.60 m wide, 3.78 m deep and 2.58 m to the beams, with the easel 2.22 m from the left wall. hfov is 70 for M5's reason: a room is painted from inside it.

_ground: The floor of a cottage, and no swell, because there is no plain: the room's own boards are what the built treatment lays under the paint.
_volume: A room, on M5's terms rather than a landscape's: the volume is not a compromise between what the paint supports and what a body wants, it *is* the room -- 4.63 m wide, 3.80 m deep and 2.59 m to the beams, off-centre because the easel stood 2.23 m from the left wall and 2.39 m from the right. The half-extents are a little inside the walls so that a viewer stops short of the plaster rather than in it.
_pacing: DESIGN 7 wants this station short as well as dark -- BUILD.md's risk table carries a row that says station 1 loses the viewer if it is too dark, too long, and gives no reason to continue, and names M6 as where that gets tested rather than argued about. One canvas is what makes it short, and the number is in BUILD.md M6.

caption.title: The Potato Eaters
caption.sub: Nuenen, April 1885. One lamp, five figures, and nothing else in the universe yet. There is no light in this room that he did not paint.
